To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have shown that the irritation caused to humans by a group of compounds, including ‘tear-gas’ (CS) and other compounds used in warfare, correlates with activation of an ion channel, hTRPA1.
the physiological activity and structure–activity relationships of solid aerosol benzylidenemalonyl cyanides in human trials are explained by their activation of TRPA1.

the potency of the irritation caused in humans by a series of solid aerosolizable benzylidenemalonyl compounds including CS, a chemical warfare agent, correlates with the potency of these compounds in activating the human transient receptor protein ankyrin 3 ion channel (hTPRA1), which is a receptor on nociceptive nerve terminals involved in the pain perception.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of TRPA1 antagonists, which are useful for treating diseases such as chronic pain, cough and asthma.
the development of a quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) for the hTRPA1 channel, which is a member of the transient receptor potential family of ion channels.
the development of novel, potent, selective and non-toxic TRPA1 channel agonists, and the use of these compounds as pharmacological tools.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the physiological activity (irritation) of the solid aerosolized compounds correlates with the activation of the TRPA channel.
the irritation caused to the human eye by the BMNs results from their reversible thiolation and subsequent activation of the TRPA channel.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown how a family of chemicals that are known to cause irritation in humans activate the human TRPA1 receptor, and that the potency of these compounds in humans correlates with their potency in vitro in human cells expressing the TRPA1 ion-channel protein.

the potency of human irritation by solid BMNs, including ‘tear gases’ (e.g., CS) and pepper sprays, correlates with their hTRPA channel activation, which is explained by the reversible thiolation of the channel by these compounds, which are dissolved in water on the surface of contaminated body tissues and penetrate cell membranes.

the potency of irritation by BMNs in humans correlates with their activation of the hTRPA1 ion channel, which is consistent with a mechanism of action involving their dissolution in body water, cell membrane penetration, and reversible thiolating of a cysteine of hTRPAI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the physiological effects of BMNs in humans are due to their activation of the TRPA 1 ion channel.
the TRPA1 ion-channel receptor is a target for the development of new treatments for human diseases.
the TRPA1 ion channels are responsible for the physiological activity of the tear gas (CS) in humans.
